blocks.text: Setting up your workspace on Mac

Since Google Sheets is a web based tool, it lacks a native Mac application. You can create a desktop shortcut to make it feel like a real app. Open Chrome and navigate to your sheet. Click the three dot menu in the top right corner. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Then click Install page as app. This creates a dedicated window that you can pin to your dock.

Speed is your goal. Use these shortcuts to save time every single hour. Press ⌘ + / to see the full list of available commands. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace text quickly. If you need to hide rows, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. For columns, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0. These small changes add up over a full work week.

Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to open find and replace
Use Option + / to open the tool finder

blocks.text: Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells. Large files can get slow if you have too many complex formulas. Try to keep your data clean. Use [remove duplicate rows](/how-to/remove-duplicate-rows-in-google-sheets) to keep your lists accurate. If you need to organize information, [freeze the top row](/how-to/freeze-the-top-row-in-google-sheets) so your headers stay visible while you scroll.

You will often receive files in CSV format. You can easily [import a CSV file](/how-to/import-a-csv-file-in-google-sheets) using the File menu. If the data is messy, use [split text into columns](/how-to/split-text-into-columns-in-google-sheets) to organize it correctly. This is often faster than typing the data by hand.
If you find yourself stuck, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a specific menu item is. It will draw a circle around the button for you.
blocks.title: Get visual help

blocks.text: Many users struggle with formula errors. Common ones include #REF! or #NAME?. Check your punctuation and cell ranges. If you have multiple Google accounts, you might see permission errors. Sign out of other accounts to keep your access clean. Use [revision history](/how-to/see-revision-history-in-google-sheets) if you accidentally delete something important.

Data entry is about consistency. Create a standard template for your sheets. Use [dropdown lists](/how-to/create-a-dropdown-list-in-google-sheets) to limit input errors. This ensures that everyone enters data in the same format. If you need to share your work, make sure you [share with view only access](/how-to/share-with-view-only-access-in-google-sheets) to protect your original file.

When you have to perform the same task repeatedly, look for ways to automate. While Sheets does not have a native macro recorder like Excel, you can use built in tools to speed up your work. Learn how to [sort data by column](/how-to/sort-data-by-column-in-google-sheets) to organize your findings. If you need to present your data, [make a chart](/how-to/make-a-chart-in-google-sheets) to visualize trends for your team.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google Sheets is a web based application. You can create a PWA shortcut in Chrome to make it open in its own window.

faq.question: How many cells can a Google Sheet hold?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, a single spreadsheet can hold up to 20 million cells.

faq.question: How can I see all keyboard shortcuts for Sheets?
faq.answer: You can view all available shortcuts by pressing ⌘ + / while inside your spreadsheet.
